men-of-all-ages-mental-health-and-workpl.core: Posted in last 7 days Men Of All Ages - Mental Health & Workplace Bullying Stories MEN, I WANT TO HEAR FROM YOU. I’m working on a new project, and I would really appreciate hearing from men who are willing to share their experiences. Why is it that men are so often expected to be strong, hold everything together, and keep their struggles to themselves? What happens when a man is being bullied or harassed at work? When he’s struggling with depression, anxiety, relationships, or simply feeling overwhelmed by life? Who does he turn to? And more importantly, does he feel comfortable asking for help? We talk so much about mental health, workplace culture, and creating environments where people feel safe speaking up. But I wonder how many men are still suffering in silence because they’re afraid of being judged, embarrassed, or seen as weak. Being strong shouldn’t mean having to suffer in silence. At the end of the day, we’re all human beings. Whether you’re a single dad raising children, a husband trying to provide for his family, a man struggling with relationships, or someone simply trying to get through another day, your feelings matter too. Being strong doesn’t mean you have to carry everything alone. I’m interested in hearing from men of all ages and backgrounds, whether you’re an employee, manager, business owner, or retired. I’m not looking for perfect answers. I’m looking for honest experiences and different perspectives. If you’ve ever felt pressure to hide what you’re going through, I’d love to hear from you. You can comment below, send me a private message, or email me at [email redacted]. I understand these are personal subjects, and I will not publicly share your name or story without your permission. My biggest question is this: What would make it easier for men to speak up without feeling like they’re losing their strength or dignity? I believe it’s time we listened more. At the end of the day, we’re all human beings. We all have struggles, emotions, and experiences that others may never see or understand. It’s not about being weak or strong. It’s about recognizing that everyone deserves to be heard. We can’t learn from one another if we’re not willing to listen. And sometimes the most important thing we can do is stop talking, open our ears, and actually hear what someone is trying to tell us. #MensMentalHealth #WorkplaceCulture #WorkplaceBullying #MentalHealthAwareness #Leadership

I'll go first I'm exceptionally good at listening I can listen to my kids talk about their problems for HOURS (and sometimes their problems are VERY serious. Someone took the wrong Minecraft sword and the world is ending) I don't judge and I don't rush to fix things. I just listen with love and genuine curiosity to understand where they come from and usually as I do this something magical happens they open up and they don't feel the need to hide things from me and often, just by talking through their problems in a space where they feel completely accepted, they discover that they already have the power to solve them I don't give them power but I help them discover their own I apply this skill to all humans I meet and as a result I managed to create the kind of partnerships for our business that would never been possible they came from listening deeply enough to understand what the other person truly needed note that i believe many man are also really good at this skill, so I am not downplaying that. I've met men who could out-listen a Buddhist monk but I do believe we've spent centuries celebrating traditionally masculine expressions of power: assertiveness, competition, control, fast decision making while we undervalue other forms of power that we might consider “fluffly”. Like empathy, patience, compassion, the ability to make others feel safe so they can just be truthful to that drives them look forward to hearing your own story in the comments
